items.type:

items.informal_description: The composition of the canonical algebra homomorphism from $ R $ to the exterior algebra $ \Lambda_R(M) $ followed by the algebra homomorphism from $ \Lambda_R(M) $ to $ R $ induced by the zero linear map on $ M $ is the identity map on $ R $.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of the Algebra Map in Exterior Algebra
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u1} [inst : CommRing R] (M : Type u2) [inst_1 : AddCommGroup M] [inst_2 : Module R M] (x : R),
  (algebraMap R (ExteriorAlgebra R M)) x = 0 ↔ x = 0
items.informal_description: The canonical algebra homomorphism from a commutative ring $ R $ to its exterior algebra $ \Lambda_R(M) $ sends an element $ x \in R $ to zero if and only if $ x $ is zero in $ R $. This establishes that the algebra map is injective.

items.informal_name: Left Inverse of Algebra Map in Tensor Algebra

In symbols, $ \mathrm{algebraMapInv} \circ \mathrm{algebraMap} = \mathrm{id}_R $.

items.informal_name: Left Inverse Equivalence for Exterior Algebra Homomorphisms
items.informal_description: For linear maps $ f: M \to N $ and $ g: N \to M $ between $ R $-modules, the induced exterior algebra homomorphisms $ \Lambda_R(f) $ and $ \Lambda_R(g) $ satisfy $ \Lambda_R(g) \circ \Lambda_R(f) = \mathrm{id} $ if and only if $ g \circ f = \mathrm{id}_M $. This establishes a bi-conditional equivalence between left inverse relationships in the original linear maps and their induced exterior algebra homomorphisms.

items.informal_name: Injectivity of the Algebra Map in Tensor Algebra
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (M : Type u_2) [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M] (x : R),
  (algebraMap R (TensorAlgebra R M)) x = 0 ↔ x = 0
items.informal_description: The canonical algebra homomorphism from a commutative semiring $ R $ to its tensor algebra $ \mathrm{TensorAlgebra}(R, M) $ is injective, as $ \mathrm{algebraMap}(x) = 0 $ if and only if $ x = 0 $ for all $ x \in R $.
